messages.subject: mdply bug?
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

Consider the following example,

library(plyr)

foo <- function(a="a", b="b", c="c", ...){
  paste(a, b, c, sep="")
  }

mdply(data.frame(b=1:4), foo)
  b  V1
1 1 1bc
2 2 2bc
3 3 3bc
4 4 4bc

It seems to me that the result is incorrect, the input variable "b"
has been interpreted as "a". If the input data.frame contains more
than one variable it works,

mdply(data.frame(b=1:4, c="c"), foo)
  b c  V1
1 1 c a1c
2 2 c a2c
3 3 c a3c
4 4 c a4c

Looks like a bug to me.

Best regards,

baptiste

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to extract information from time series data arranged in a
3-dimensional array: each column contains a time series, with
different columns of a matrix representing measurements in different
channels. Each matrix along the third dimension represents different
trials.

I would like to extract different parameters (like mean, max, min...)
from consecutive sub-intervals of each time series (e.g., the maximum
value within the first 100ms, the second 100ms, etc.) for each channel
and trial. The result should be arranged in a data frame with the
columns holding the extracted parameter per channel/time-interval
combination and the rows representing the different trials.

With a little help from a colleague I have ended up with a solution
which involves three different 'for'-statements (see below). I have
tried simplifying the code somewhat with 'apply' and 'plyr'-functions,
but (lacking proper manipulatr skills) haven't been successful. Hence
my first question:

- Is there a way to simplify the code and make it more efficient using
apply/plyr/reshape functions?

And a second question:

- When I try to extract the time points (indexes) of maxima/minima
within each sub-interval using 'which.max'/'which.min', R returns the
time points relative to each sub-interval (which would always be '5'
and '1', respectively, if done for the example below). While I want to
get this information for each sub-interval, I would like to get the
absolute indexes within the whole time series. Does anybody have a
suggestion of how to do this?

The code is given below, I'll be happy about any suggestions!

Many thanks,

Philip

Here's the code:

## set up an example array and the names for the columns (=channels
"A" and "B")

t<-array(1:120, c(20,2,3))

dimnames(t)<-list(NULL, c("A", "B"), NULL)

## define length of intervals from which to extract parameters, set up
an empty data frame and name its
## columns (where the bit before the separator indicates the channels
and the number after the separator the
## index of the respective time interval)

interval=5

df<-as.data.frame(rep(list(V=double(0)), times=ncol(t)*(nrow(t)/
interval)))

colnames(df)<-paste(rep(colnames(t), times=nrow(t)/interval), rep(1:
(nrow(t)/interval), each=ncol(t)), sep=".")

## fill the data frame column by column and row by row with the
relevant parameters extracted from the
## data array

for (i in 1:(nrow(t)/interval))
for (k in 1:ncol(t))
for (r in 1:length(t[1,1,]))
{ df[r , (i-1)*ncol(t) + k] = max(t[((i-1)*interval+1) : (i*interval),
k, r]) }

## this is what the data frame looks like

    A.1  B.1 A.2  B.2  A.3  B.3 A.4 B.4
1    5   25   10   30   15   35   20   40
2   45   65   50   70   55   75   60   80
3   85  105   90  110   95  115  100  120

If the desired output is a data frame, it's easiest (but not
efficient) to convert the array to a data frame and work with that:

t <- array(1:120, c(20,2,3))
dimnames(t) <- list(NULL, c("A", "B"), NULL)

library(reshape)
tdf <- melt(t)
tdf$slice <- round_any(tdf$X1, 5, floor)

summary <- ddply(tdf, c("slice", "X2", "X3"), summarise,
  mean = mean(value), max = max(value))

recast(summary, slice ~ X2 + X3 | variable, id.var = c("slice", "X2", "X3"))

data easier to work with without the recast - generally it's much
easier to work with data frames in R because they have observation
labels as columns, rather than in another data structure (e.g. as with
dimnames).

For your second question, there's no easy way because indices are
inherently relative.  It would be easier with a data frame because you
could save all the index columns.

Hadley
